prerequisites: A fresh DOC-030 access-2 Administrator account invited by the seeded Administrator (Daniel Okafor) through the API, with its Set your OpenLaw password email read from the lab Mailpit.
Test preparation only: the account's first invitation token was expired in the lab database, on this walkthrough's own row, to exercise refusal.
A second browser context for the other-device, revoked-session and password-reset checks. The expired-link re-walk used another fresh account of the same role.
scenarios.expected: The intended account reaches its permitted landing page; two-factor and session controls have their documented effects. Expired activation, incorrect password/code, and revoked-session behavior are observable without exposing another account.
scenarios.actual: 25 recorded Administrator steps passed. An Administrator invite sent Set your OpenLaw password with a Set password control, the line The link expires in one hour., and the token in the URL fragment. An expired link showed This link has expired or was already used. Ask for a new one. Opening /auth/set-password without the fragment showed This link is not valid. Ask for a new invitation or password reset. After a fresh invitation, a mismatch showed The passwords do not match. Set password then showed Password set with Sign in. The sign-in page showed Helix Software Group above the Sign in heading and form and no logo, which matches the public branding (no logo saved). A wrong password showed Check your email and password. The right one landed on /. The name menu showed the name and email, and the header showed Helix Software Group at 1440 px but not at 700 px. The used invitation link was refused. Turn on two-factor took Password, then a QR code and manual secret. A wrong Code was refused, and Confirm showed 10 backup codes. After Done, Profile said two-factor is on. At Two-factor authentication a wrong code showed Wrong code. Try again, or restart sign-in., and the current code with Verify reached /. A backup code worked once and its reuse was refused. Sign out on the challenge restarted sign-in. Sign out other devices sent a second browser to sign-in while this one stayed. An abandoned Re-enroll left two-factor off. Turn off two-factor refused a wrong password with Check your password., then worked with the right one. Email me a sign-in link with Send link showed Check your email. Sign in to OpenLaw (5 minutes) signed in once, and the reused link opened Sign-in link expired. Re-walk against the corrected paragraph: with sign-in links on (the real lab setting), that page showed Email and Send link and no Back to sign-in, and Send link gave a new link that signed in. With links off, mocked in the browser only, it showed only Back to sign-in, which returned to sign-in, and password sign-in worked. The fourth sign-in link request showed Too many sign-in link requests. Try again later. Set up or reset your password sent a 60-minute link. Password set ended a session held by another browser, the old password was refused, and the new one worked. The fourth setup request showed Too many password setup requests. Try again later. Nine wrong passwords then a correct one cleared the counter. After 10 wrong codes across two challenges, the next attempt, and the current code, showed Too many attempts. Wait 15 minutes, then try again. After 10 wrong passwords, the next attempt and the correct password showed the same message. An ineligible address got the same Check your email page for both requests and no email. Supplementary mocked checks rendered Continue with single sign-on, Single sign-on is not configured yet and Administrator sign-in (which opens the password form).

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the author and technical reviewer. It is not a human user study and not the feature owner's approval.

The work2 lab (openlaw-docs-80ceef9e-work2, source 067c1646829df85e62b809ee9157921e867c84e7, Helix seed light profile, random seed 7) is shared with other DOC-030 agents. Only doc030.access2.* throwaway accounts were created, and no organization setting was changed. One throwaway account was archived by this walkthrough. The lab runs with AUTH_RATE_LIMIT=off, but the lockouts and email budgets are database counters and were observed.

The first run (10:31-10:35 UTC) walked guide bytes 6a8ac93d. Its expired-link step failed on both roles because the page had no Back to sign-in while sign-in links were on. The author then corrected only that paragraph (29d19f72). The step was walked again for both roles at 10:41-10:45 UTC. walkthrough.json keeps the failed records under supersededSteps. Every other step keeps its first-run observation, because the rest of the guide text did not change (git diff: one line).

Required two-factor authentication (the organization policy, Your organization requires two-factor authentication. and Required by your organization) was not exercised: it needs an organization-wide policy change on the shared lab.

Single sign-on, Administrator sign-in, Password sign-in is disabled for this account. and Sign-in link expired with sign-in links off need organization-wide policy changes. They were checked only as browser rendering with a mocked methods answer. No live identity provider was used.
The seeded organization has no saved logo, so only the no-logo branch was observed live.
The five-minute sign-in link expiry was not waited out; used-link refusal was observed. The one-hour password setup token lifetime was read from the lab database.
An Administrator landing on unfinished organization setup was not exercised, because the lab onboarding is complete. The OAuth Client sign-in return (M41) is left to the Connect guides.
The per-client-address budget of 30 sign-in link requests in 15 minutes is shared by every agent on this lab; the walkthrough waited for room instead of exhausting it.
